Bearer.description: The instance password (root: every route) or a scoped token: a token answers only the routes whose scope it carries.

info.description: Self-hosted, single-user expense tracker. Capture is separate from organizing: a capture parks something unconfirmed, and only an approval writes a ledger entry.
info.title: Spenicle API

get.description: Balances are in the account's own currency, `base_amount_minor` in the base currency. Filters widen: a `* list` parameter takes comma-separated values.

parameters.description: true only archived, false only live
parameters.name: archived

get.summary: Every account with the balance the ledger implies

post.description: `kind` decides what it is: asset, liability, equity, expense or income. A missing `currency` inherits the base currency; a `parent_ref` must name an existing account.
post.summary: Create an account or a category

patch.description: Send absolute values only; an omitted field is left alone. Archiving is `archived: true` and never deletes the row.
patch.summary: Rename, re-icon, reparent or archive an account

get.description: `rollup=parent` rolls a child category into its parent. `bucket=month` answers `bucketedCategoryAnalyticsResponse` instead, one series per category.
get.summary: Spend per category for a range

post.description: A saved view is a name, a namespace and a chart kind; running it reuses the analytics routes.

get.description: Answers the namespace's own shape: `months` for the monthly namespace, `categories` for the category one.
get.summary: Run a saved view over a window

patch.description: Absolute values only; the namespace is fixed once saved.
patch.summary: Rename or re-chart a saved view

get.description: Every month in the window is present, including the empty ones. Money is minor units as strings.
get.summary: Spend and income per calendar month

get.description: Append-only and newest first. `payload` carries the recorded shape of the change; a ref is never resolved to a name.

parameters.description: created, updated, reversed, revoked and friends
parameters.name: action

get.summary: The journal: what changed, who changed it

get.description: The one read a client needs before it holds a credential. It answers in open mode, in gate mode and in normal mode, and it never carries a credential, an account, an amount or a secret. `setup_completed` says whether `POST /api/setup` still has to run, `password_must_change` whether the first-boot password still has to be replaced.
get.summary: Public boot state: is the ledger opened, is the password still the generated one?

get.description: Pending first. A capture is unconfirmed by definition: only an approval writes an entry.
get.summary: The review queue

post.description: Writes no ledger entry: a capture is the two-second capture path. `202` when it is parked for extraction, `200` when `idempotency_key` replayed a stored capture.

patch.description: `action` picks the branch: `approve` posts a balanced entry and answers `201` with the entry beside the capture, `reject` closes it, `retry` re-runs extraction, `match` links it to an entry that already exists.
patch.summary: Approve, reject, retry or match a capture

get.description: The bytes are gzipped when compressible and encrypted under `APP_SECRET`; the row is metadata, the file is the document. `410` once the retention sweep reclaimed it.
get.summary: Download the document behind a capture

get.description: A rule maps a pattern, a field and a match kind to one category; the highest priority wins.
get.summary: The deterministic category rules, oldest first

post.description: The category must exist and be an expense or income account. Rules are deterministic: the same input always suggests the same category.
post.summary: Teach one rule: a pattern, a field and a category

patch.description: Absolute values only. Archiving keeps the row and its journal entry.
patch.summary: Repoint, reprioritise or archive a rule

get.description: `tier` says which layer answered: an explicit rule, the payee default, or the fallback category.
get.summary: The category this payee or text would get, and why

get.description: Answers `disconnected` when no grant is stored; the secrets never leave the sealed row.
get.summary: The current Google mailbox connection, or `disconnected`

post.description: Writes the client id and secret into the sealed row and answers the URL the browser must visit. The secret is never echoed back.
post.summary: Store OAuth client credentials and start authorisation

get.description: Public route: the browser arrives here with `code` and `state`, not with a credential. An unknown or replayed `state` is refused.
get.summary: Finish the Google grant from the browser redirect

post.description: Marks the connection revoked; a capture that already arrived keeps its evidence.
post.summary: Disconnect the stored grant, keep the row

get.description: One round trip for the screen: the window totals, the month series, the pending capture count and the biggest category.
get.summary: The landing tiles in one response

get.description: Filters widen the result: every `* list` parameter takes one value or many, comma-separated. `amount_min` and `amount_max` compare the absolute base-currency posting amount. A `limit` above 200 is refused, never clamped.

parameters.description: occurred_on >= from; YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM in APP_TIMEZONE
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: occurred_on <= to; a bare date covers the whole day
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: substring of the note or of the payee name
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: true only reversed entries, false only live ones, absent both
parameters.name: reversed

parameters.description: smallest absolute posting amount to match

parameters.description: largest absolute posting amount to match

parameters.name: with_balance

get.summary: List the ledger, newest first

post.description: The only way money enters the ledger. Native and base sums must both be zero; a posting without `fx_rate` is converted with the resolved rate, and the result is rounded once, half away from zero. Replaying `idempotency_key` returns the stored entry with `200` instead of posting a second one.

requestBody.description: the request body | the entry to post

200.description: the idempotency_key replayed a stored entry

get.description: A reversed entry still answers and carries `reversed_at`; the reversal is a separate entry.
get.summary: One entry with its postings

patch.description: One body action per call: `reverse: true` writes the reversal (the original stays), `payee_ref` repoints, `occurred_on`, `note` and `postings` replace the entry in place.
patch.summary: Reverse an entry or correct it

get.description: The way a client watches the queue; `format` and `status` narrow the listing.

parameters.description: queued, running, ready, failed or expired
parameters.name: status

get.summary: Every export job, newest first

post.description: A job, not a request: this answers `201` with a queued row and the worker renders it. A `idempotency_key` replay answers `200` with the same job; the same key and another `format` is `409 export_conflict`.

get.description: A `ready` job past retention answers `410 gone` from the download route; the row stays.
get.summary: One export job and its progress

get.description: One JSON document, or a zip of CSV sheets plus `summary.json` and `manifest.json`. The download is recorded as an event; a `ready` job past retention is `410 gone` and a blob already swept is not an error.
get.summary: Stream the rendered document

get.description: `queued`, `resumed`, `started`, `completed`, `failed`, `downloaded`, `expired`, `swept`; the actor says whether the user or the worker wrote it.
get.summary: The append-only log of one export job

get.description: A draft holds its rows for 24h past the last edit; a committed or rejected batch keeps its evidence forever.
get.summary: Every statement batch, newest first

post.description: Two-phase: this route writes a draft and nothing reaches the ledger until `PATCH /api/imports/{ref}` commits it. Send the whole file, or a chunk per call with `chunk_index` and `chunk_total`; the last chunk assembles the draft. The same `idempotency_key` with the same bytes resumes the draft (`200`), with different bytes it is `409 import_conflict`.

account_ref.description: the account every row is posted against

post.summary: Upload a CSV statement as a reviewable draft

get.description: Each row carries its own clash verdict: `already_imported`, `duplicate`, `possible_duplicate` or `invalid_row`.
get.summary: One batch with its rows

patch.description: `commit` posts the accepted rows, each under `import:<file_hash>:<row_index>`, which makes a replay a no-op. `reject` closes the draft and keeps the evidence.
patch.summary: Commit the draft or reject it, one body action

get.description: `uploaded`, `resumed`, `conflict_refused`, `row_edited`, `row_accepted`, `row_skipped`, `committed`, `rejected`, `expired`; the actor says whether the user or the worker wrote it.
get.summary: The append-only log of one batch

patch.description: Absolute values only, so a retry changes nothing. An edit extends the draft's `expires_at` and records the edited fields; a row edit while `committing` is `409 import_committing`.
patch.summary: Edit, accept or skip one drafted row

get.description: Whether polling is on and which senders are allowed; the mailbox credentials stay sealed.
get.summary: The intake configuration, never its secrets

patch.description: Absolute values only: the whole allowlist is replaced. The worker polls on its next run.
patch.summary: Turn polling on, set the sender allowlist

get.description: Newest first, one row per observed message, each carrying the capture it produced.
get.summary: Every message seen by intake

get.description: The handle and message id are kept as evidence; the body is not stored here.
get.summary: One observed message and the capture it produced

post.description: Re-runs the sync for one handle; a superseded message stays in the listing.
post.summary: Re-read one message from the provider

post.description: Same path the worker runs. Every message either becomes a capture or is recorded with its skip reason; nothing is posted to the ledger.

get.description: Everything the shell needs before its first screen, in one response.
get.summary: Bootstrap payload: settings, accounts, payees, recurring rules, currencies

post.description: Root credential only. The old password must match; the new one is at least 12 characters and is stored as a PBKDF2 hash inside the sealed settings row. An optional `token` mints the browser credential in the same call, so a first boot costs one request instead of two; like `POST /api/tokens`, the plaintext exists exactly once, in this response. The first-boot secret file is removed once the change lands.

get.description: Newest first, paged by cursor.

parameters.description: true only archived, false only live
parameters.name: archived

get.summary: Every payee with its default accounts

post.description: The default account and category prefill a capture approval; both must name an existing row.
post.summary: Create a payee with optional defaults

patch.description: Absolute values only; `archived: true` hides the payee from a prefill without deleting it.
patch.summary: Rename, re-default or archive a payee

get.description: Answers from the in-memory cache, then the stored sheet for that exact day, then the nearest earlier day, then a cross rate through EUR. `on` defaults to today in `APP_TIMEZONE`.

parameters.description: the day to price, default today
parameters.name: on

get.summary: The cached ECB reference rate for one day

get.description: `state` narrows to active or paused rules; a `* list` parameter widens with comma-separated values.
get.summary: Every recurring rule, soonest due first

post.description: The worker queues a capture for each due rule and never posts an entry: an approval still writes the ledger.

patch.description: Absolute values only. Pausing is `state: paused`; the row and its journal entries stay.

get.description: Never carries the password hash or the secret. `extraction_enabled` and `ai_assistance` say which rails are wired.
get.summary: The in-app settings the shell reads

patch.description: The base currency and the timezone are fixed at the first boot: this route answers `422 empty_patch` and changes nothing.
patch.summary: Discover that no setting is patchable

post.description: Completes once: it locks the base currency and every opening balance. Opening balances are posted as one balanced entry per account.
post.summary: Open the ledger with a base currency and optional opening balances

get.description: Newest first. `status` and `used` narrow the listing; the preview is the only thing that identifies a token.
get.summary: Every issued token, never its secret

post.description: The plaintext exists exactly once, in this response. Only its HMAC digest and a masked preview are stored; the scopes decide which scoped routes it answers.
`revoked_at` stamps the row, the credential stops authenticating immediately, and the journal keeps the entry.
post.summary: Revoke a token; the row stays

get.description: Answers `degraded` when the store cannot be reached. The `app_secret` value is a fingerprint, never the secret. Public route: no credential is read.
get.summary: Liveness, build and schema fingerprint
